name: web/animation-2d
title: 2D animation
summary: One HTML page with one animation drawn on a plain 2D canvas, with no library and no internet: bouncing balls, sea waves, planets around a sun, fireworks, rain or an analogue clock.
when: Use when the user wants a 2D animation or moving picture for the browser: bouncing balls, waves, planets, fireworks, rain or a clock. Not for anything in 3D.

title.about: The name of the animation, shown at the top left and in the browser tab.

kind.about: What moves: balls (bouncing balls under gravity), waves, orbits (planets around a sun), fireworks, rain or clock. A whole sentence works; the first of these words found is used.

color.about: The main color of the animation, as a CSS color name or a hex code; leaving it own lets the animation choose a color that fits it.

count.about: How many things are drawn (balls, wave layers, planets, rockets or raindrops), as a plain number. The clock ignores it.

background.about: The background of the page, as a CSS color name or a hex code; leaving it own lets the animation choose a background that fits it.

next: Nothing more to do: the page is finished and shows itself in the chat. Do not read it, run it, build it or install anything; tell the user in one or two sentences what the animation shows. Only when the user asks for a change: edit the plain lines at the top of index.html inside <script type="text/plain" id="settings"> with replace_in_file, one line per call.
change: Only the four lines at the top of index.html, inside <script type="text/plain" id="settings">, are edited: kind, color, count, background. One call per change, copying the old line exactly: replace_in_file(path="{file}", old="color #5fd3c4", new="color teal").

not_text: Not a known kind, so bouncing balls are shown. Known kinds: balls, waves, orbits, fireworks, rain, clock.
Not a color the page knows, so the default color is used.
Not a background color the page knows, so the background of that kind is used.
